newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO NIKKEI ENDS BELOW 19,500, 1ST TIME IN 3 MTHS.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO NIKKEI ENDS BELOW 19,500, 1ST TIME IN 3 MTHS.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed lower on Thursday, with the key market index finishing below the 19,500 level for the first time since May 1.
The benchmark index briefly dropped more than 1.5 percent, as aggressive sales of certain construction sector shares cast a pall over the market, brokers said.
Underlying worries that Japan's economy may not start picking up soon were reinforced by slowing demand in Japan's personal computer market, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average closed down 226.22 points or 1.15 percent at 19,475.85. It briefly slid as low as 19,366.14. September Nikkei futures fell 380 points to end at 19,370.
Shares of debt-burdened construction firms tumbled and some hit record lows, as investors rushed to cut their losses.

"Construction shares that have been left weak in the recent polarised trade just don't stop falling. Anxiety over their financial health is behind the declines," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.

The market was also damaged by waning optimism over major Japanese industries, as weaker domestic demand for personal computers hurt technology shares and recent discouraging car data has weighed on shares of automakers, brokers said.
"Many people hoped the economy would be recovering this fall, but now we are worried that the sluggishness may last longer," said Dai-Ichi Securities analyst Akishige Ishikura.
Turnover was a modest 378 million shares on Thursday, against 392 million traded on Wednesday. Losers outnumbered winners 869 to 228, while 155 issues were unchanged.
The broader-based TOPIX index lost 10.53 points or 0.70 percent to end at 1,497.10. The Nikkei 300 index retreated 1.80 points or 0.61 percent to 293.03.

The top three percentage losers on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) were construction companies, with Sato Kogyo Co Ltd listed at the top, followed by Sata Construction Co Ltd and Fujita Corp.
Sato Kogyo shed 25 yen or 18.52 percent to end at 110 yen after briefly hitting 108 yen, a new low for 1997.
Sata gave up 40 yen or 18.18 percent to close at 180 yen, also a new low for this calendar year.
Fujita lost 21 yen or 18.10 percent to end at 95 yen. It slipped as low as 92 yen, a record low. Its volume of 7.473 million shares was the second-heaviest on the first section.
Brokers said that while there were no new developments which prompted the selling, investors were discouraged that prices of construction shares were showing no signs of recovery.
Computer makers slipped further. Worries that domestic computer demand may be on the wane somewhat eclipsed overnight news of a linkup between Microsoft Corp and Apple Computer Inc.

The Japan Electronic Industry Development Association said on Thursday that shipments of personal computers in the April-June period showed a meagre rise of four percent from the same period last year to 1.7 million units.
In contrast, PC shipments in the same period last year had shown a 51 percent increase year-on-year. Fujitsu fell 40 yen to 1,670 and NEC fell 30 yen to 1,630.
Elimination of cross shareholdings hit major steelmaker NKK Corp, bringing it to a new low for the year of 195 yen. It closed 10 yen lower at 197.
Basic industries, including steel, were also hurt by worries about the economy's slowing down, brokers said.
Banks, however, rose on short-covering. The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan rose 36 yen to 570, with its volume of 9.973 million shares the biggest on the TSE.
"News on Wednesday that Japan was approving issuance of perpetual bonds by corporations ignited the short-covering," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
By sector, losers were led by mining, air transport, gas, construction and fisheries. The major gainers were precision instruments, communications, banks and retailers.
The second section index fell 8.56 points to close at 1,699.73, with 7.37 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 7.92 points at 1,087.75.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
